title: Command-Line Calculator
goal: Build a calculator that reads two numbers and an operator from the user, then prints the result.
requirements: Ask the user for two numbers and an operator (+, -, *, /)
Perform the correct calculation based on the operator
Handle division by zero without crashing
architecture: Read three inputs -> convert the numbers with float() -> use if/elif to pick the operation -> print the result.
milestones: Read and print the two numbers back to confirm input works
hints: input() always returns a string — convert it with float() before doing math.
Check for the divide-by-zero case before performing the division.
commonProblems: Forgetting to convert input() results to numbers, causing a TypeError when adding them.
Not handling an unrecognized operator symbol.
testingChecklist: 10 / 0 shows a friendly message instead of crashing
extensions: Loop so the user can do multiple calculations without restarting the program

title: Number Guessing Game
goal: The computer picks a secret number; the player guesses until they get it right, receiving 'too high'/'too low' feedback.
requirements: Count and report the number of guesses when the player wins
architecture: Import random -> generate a secret number -> loop reading a guess each time -> compare and give feedback -> break on a correct guess.
milestones: Hardcode the secret number and get the win condition working
Track and display the guess count
hints: random.randint(1, 100) gives a random whole number from 1 to 100 inclusive.
Convert the guess to int() before comparing it to the secret number.
commonProblems: Comparing a string guess to an int secret number without converting first.
Loop never ending because the win condition doesn't break out.
testingChecklist: Guessing correctly on the first try ends the game immediately
Guesses outside 1-100 are still handled gracefully
extensions: Add a difficulty setting that changes the number range

title: Simple Expense Tracker
goal: Track a list of expenses in memory and print a running total and category breakdown.
requirements: Store each expense as a dictionary with amount and category
architecture: Keep a list of expense dictionaries -> loop to add entries -> loop again to sum totals overall and per category.
milestones: Store and print a single expense
Support multiple expenses in a list
Calculate totals per category using a dictionary
hints: A dictionary like {"amount": 12.5, "category": "food"} is a clean way to represent one expense.
Use dict.get(key, 0) to safely add to a running per-category total.
commonProblems: Forgetting that dictionary keys are case-sensitive when grouping categories.
Not initializing a category's running total before adding to it.
testingChecklist: Adding three expenses in the same category sums correctly
An empty expense list reports a total of 0 without crashing
extensions: Save expenses to a JSON file so they persist between runs
Add a monthly budget and warn when it's exceeded
